title: The Chisel Crosses the Ocean: a Friulian Sculptor and the Stone Face of Buenos Aires
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buja, birth in the Friulian hills
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day are given by no source and are defaulted to January 1
stops.campa: In 1885, in Buja, a scatter of farm hamlets in the hills above the Udine plain, Troiano Troiani is born. Friuli in these decades sends its young men across the Atlantic by the shipload, to the quarries and the railway cuttings of the Americas, and the wheat and the silk that stay behind do not hold the villages together. Troiani will make the crossing too, with a chisel instead of a pick. No source names the house he is born in. The town is the only fixed point at the beginning of him.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani
Wikidata Q110846062
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buja (coordinates 46 13 N, 13 08 E)
suggested_refs: The commune of Buja, province of Udine; Wikidata records the birthplace at province level and Spanish Wikipedia at town level, an ambiguity left standing

stops.name: Venice, the first discipline under Anibal de Lotto
stops.date_confidence: undated in every source reached; placed in the 1900s and defaulted to January 1, 1900
stops.campa: Troiani learns sculpture in Venice, under Anibal de Lotto. The city gives him plaster casts of antiquity, facades standing in tidewater, and a master with a name in Italian academic circles. Which academy or private studio holds the lessons, the record does not say; it names the city and the teacher and stops there. Hands raised among Friulian wheat are set here to armature wire and wet clay, and the sequence begins that will carry him to Florence, to Rome, to Austria, and then off the continent altogether.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani
suggested_refs: The Accademia di Belle Arti di Venezia, used here as a landmark coordinate only; no source confirms it as Troiani's school

stops.name: Florence, the weight of precedent
stops.date_confidence: undated; the sequence is attested, the years are not, and this is a placeholder within the decade
stops.campa: From Venice he goes on to Florence, where the academies and the galleries have been telling Italian sculptors what sculpture is for four hundred years. No institution and no teacher is named for him here; only the city. Florence adds to the Venetian lessons the pressure of precedent, marble already worked by men whose names every student in the city is made to recite before he is allowed to touch stone. Troiani does not settle. Rome comes next, Austria after Rome, and the ocean after Austria.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani
suggested_refs: The Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze, a plausible landmark for the Florentine years, not confirmed as his school

stops.name: Rome, the antique lying thick on the ground
stops.date_confidence: undated; the city is attested and the year is a placeholder within the decade
stops.campa: Rome is the third station of his training, named in the record without an academy, a teacher, or an address attached to it. It is the city where the antique lies thickest on the ground, where generations of European sculptors have been sent to learn the anatomy of a torso and the geometry of falling drapery from the fragments themselves. Whatever Troiani takes from it travels with him. Twenty years later a classical vocabulary learned somewhere in these streets will dress the banks and the legislature of a republic in the southern hemisphere.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani
suggested_refs: A general historic-centre point stands in for Rome; no academy or teacher is named in any source, an open gap

stops.name: Vienna, the last European lesson
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the source names only the country, Austria, with no city, school, teacher, or year
stops.campa: The account of his European formation ends with a single word, Austria, and nothing after it. Vienna, with its Akademie der bildenden Kunste, is the natural continuation of Venice, Florence and Rome, and it stands here as reconstruction rather than fact; no source reached names any Austrian city, school or master. He meets the currents running through European art in these years without joining the avant-garde movements carrying them. Whatever the Austrian lesson is, it is the last one taught to him on this continent.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (names Austria only)
suggested_refs: The Akademie der bildenden Kunste, Vienna, offered as reconstruction; the Italian-side account in Giuseppe Bergamini's Dizionario biografico dei friulani entry could not be reached (server errors)

stops.name: Genoa, the embarkation for the River Plate
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month, day, port and vessel are all unknown, and the port itself is unresolved between two candidates
stops.campa: In 1910 Troiani boards a ship for Buenos Aires. No source reached names the port, the vessel or the day. Genoa is the great embarkation quay for northern Italians in these years and stands here as the likelier of two candidates; the other is Trieste, far closer to Friuli but not Italian in 1910, being then the principal port of Austria-Hungary and annexed to Italy only after the war. Friuli lies on that frontier. Which quay he walked down is left open rather than closed by preference.
sources: No direct source; inference from Friulian emigration patterns of the period, explicitly unconfirmed
suggested_refs: Passenger manifests of the Genoa and Trieste lines to the River Plate, 1910, unconsulted

stops.name: Retiro, the landing at the port of Buenos Aires
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the landing point is reconstruction, since no source places Troiani at Retiro at all
stops.campa: Immigrants of 1910 come ashore at Retiro, where the state keeps its reception buildings along the port. The great pavilion of the Hotel de Inmigrantes is still under construction, its doors opening only in 1911, so an arrival of this year passes through an older facility on the same stretch of water. No document places Troiani on that quay; the landing is inferred from the year and from where ships of his kind put in. What is attested is plainer. He arrives, and he never goes back to live in Friuli.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (year and scholarship attested)
Hotel de Inmigrantes, Av. Antartida Argentina 1355, built 1906-1911, pavilion opened 1911
suggested_refs: Argentine immigration registers for 1910, which would settle the vessel and the date, unconsulted

stops.name: Parque 3 de Febrero, the Centennial year
stops.date_confidence: the Centennial date is attested; Troiani's presence on the exhibition grounds is nowhere recorded
stops.campa: The year Troiani lands is the year Buenos Aires marks a century since the May revolution, with international exhibitions laid across the Palermo parkland to announce the republic to the world. The scholarship that brought him south belongs to the same undertaking: a country building monuments to itself needs hands trained in Venice, Florence and Rome to cut them. Whether he walks the exhibition grounds is not recorded anywhere. The Centennial is the weather his arrival happens in, not a stop on his own itinerary.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (the government scholarship scheme for European artists)
suggested_refs: The 1910 Centennial exhibitions in the Palermo parkland, context for the scholarship scheme that brought him

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the oath of citizenship
stops.date_confidence: the naturalization is attested; its year, month, day and registering office are given by no source, and this date is a placeholder carrying no weight
stops.campa: At some point after his arrival Troiani is naturalized an Argentine citizen. The proceeding leaves no date and no office in any source reached; only the fact of it survives. The scholarship that carried him across becomes residence, then nationality, and the Friulian is now legally what he will remain, an Argentine who decorates Argentina. He spends fifty-three years in this city and dies in it, and the stone he cuts for its banks and its legislature outlasts every paper the naturalization generated.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (naturalization attested, undated)
suggested_refs: Argentine naturalization records of the 1910s, unconsulted; the date and office are an open gap

stops.name: Bolsa de Comercio, the exchange dressed in stone
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January 1
stops.campa: In 1916 Troiani cuts sculptural decoration for the new Bolsa de Comercio at Leandro N. Alem and 25 de Mayo, the Beaux-Arts exchange raised by Alejandro Christophersen between 1913 and 1916. He works beside another sculptor, Riganti. Six years after the ship, the training of four Italian cities goes onto the front of a building where the wheat of the pampas is priced. The exchange's own record of itself names no sculptors at all; the credit comes from the sculptor's side of the ledger, not the building's.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (Troiani and Riganti)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsa_de_Comercio_de_Buenos_Aires (Christophersen, 1913-1916, Av. L. N. Alem 356 / 25 de Mayo 367)
Wikidata Q110846062 (works held at the Bolsa)
suggested_refs: The Bolsa de Comercio building, Av. Leandro N. Alem 356; the sculptural credit rests on the biography page alone, a single-source attribution

stops.name: Teatro Grand Splendid, sculpture under the painted dome
stops.date_confidence: the theater opens in May 1919; no source gives any date for Troiani's work there, and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: On Avenida Santa Fe the Grand Splendid opens in May 1919, a theater and picture palace by Pero and Torres Armengol, its dome painted in oil by Nazareno Orlandi as an allegory of peace at the close of the war. Troiani supplies a sculptural ensemble for it. The theater's own account of itself names the painter and no sculptor; the attribution comes from artedelaargentina, the very reference the biographical article leans on. No year attaches to his part. The building survives, converted into a bookshop, and the ensemble with it.
sources: artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (sculptural ensemble for the Teatro Grand Splendid)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Ateneo_Grand_Splendid (Av. Santa Fe 1860, May 1919, Pero y Torres Armengol, Orlandi dome; names no sculptor)
suggested_refs: The Grand Splendid interior at Av. Santa Fe 1860; the sculptural ensemble is credited by artedelaargentina and by no encyclopedic article

stops.name: Banco Tornquist, the second temple of money
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, and the building's exact address is a reconstruction
stops.campa: In 1927 Troiani supplies sculpture for a building of the house of Tornquist, one of the great private banking names of Buenos Aires, in the financial blocks near Reconquista. The year and the commission are attested; no source reached names the structure or its address, and the placement in the Microcentro rests only on where the firm is known to have sat. Eleven years after the exchange, the same classical idiom is cut for the same clientele. The republic's money keeps asking for gods and keeps hiring a Friulian to carve them.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (year and commission attested)
suggested_refs: The Tornquist banking house buildings of the Microcentro; the specific structure Troiani decorated is unidentified, an open gap

stops.name: Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, the chair of sculpture
stops.date_confidence: the post is attested and undated; no source gives a start year and this one is inferred from his arrival
stops.campa: Troiani teaches sculpture on Avenida Las Heras for decades, at the school the state nationalised in 1905 out of workshops the Sociedad Estimulo de Bellas Artes had run since 1878. He forms, the record says, several generations of artists. Not one of them is named. The school's own history does not mention him either; the post survives on the strength of the biography alone. A boy out of Buja stands in front of the room and teaches a capital how to build a figure in clay before it goes to the foundry.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (teaching post attested)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escuela_Nacional_de_Bellas_Artes_Prilidiano_Pueyrredon (1878 workshops, 1905 nationalisation, Av. Las Heras 1749; does not name Troiani)
suggested_refs: Staff registers of the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes; no student of Troiani's is named in any source reached, an open gap

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Salon Nacional
stops.date_confidence: participation is attested in general terms only; no year, medal or exhibited work is named in any source, and this date is a placeholder
stops.campa: Troiani shows at the Salon Nacional, the republic's official exhibition of painting and sculpture, and shows there successfully; he holds individual exhibitions as well. That is the whole of what the record gives. No year is named, no medal, no title of any piece he hung or set on a plinth. A career of public commissions is documented street by street and building by building, and the exhibition life running alongside it for forty years survives as a single adjective.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (successful participation in the Salon Nacional and in individual exhibitions)
suggested_refs: Salon Nacional catalogues, which would supply years, works and awards; unconsulted, and the single largest documentary gap in his career

stops.name: Palais de Glace, the Salon after 1932
stops.date_confidence: the venue housed the Salon from 1932 to 1954 and again from 1960; no catalogue reached places Troiani there in any given year
stops.campa: From 1932 the Salon Nacional is held in the Palais de Glace on Posadas, a former ice rink in Recoleta turned over to the national exhibition, and there it stays until 1954 before returning in 1960. Troiani has been exhibiting since the 1910s, so for the first two decades of his showing the venue is categorically somewhere else. This entry covers the later half of the habit only, and even for that half no catalogue reached names him in any particular year.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_de_Glace (Salon Nacional held there 1932-1954 and from 1960)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (participation attested in general terms)
suggested_refs: The Palais de Glace, Posadas 1725; the venue link for Troiani is reconstruction, and is invalid for his pre-1932 exhibiting

stops.name: Las Heras 1749, the school takes Pueyrredon's name
stops.date_confidence: Decree 72154 of 1940 is attested; the month and day of the decree are not carried in the source
stops.campa: By decree in 1940 the Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes takes the name of the painter Prilidiano Pueyrredon. Troiani has by then been teaching under the older name for thirty years, and the summaries that call him a professor of the Prilidiano Pueyrredon across his whole tenure are reading a name backwards into decades that never held it. The rooms are the same, and so are the students at the modelling stands. Only the letterhead changes, and every later account of him changes with it.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escuela_Nacional_de_Bellas_Artes_Prilidiano_Pueyrredon (Decree 72154 of 1940)
suggested_refs: Decree 72154 of 1940, which renamed the Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes; the anachronism it creates runs through most summaries of Troiani's career

stops.name: Champagne, the lamps cast in France
stops.date_confidence: no source gives any year for the commission; this date is an arbitrary bracket midpoint, and the foundry town is unknown
stops.campa: The fifty-one lamps for the Plaza de los Dos Congresos are not made in Buenos Aires. They are cast in the Champagne region of France, under Troiani's own direction, in artistic ironwork of one to five arms apiece. The foundry town is named in no source reached, and neither is the year. A sculptor out of Friuli, employed by an Argentine republic, crosses back into Europe to stand over French furnaces so that a plaza in the southern hemisphere can be lit by wrought iron.
sources: artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (51 artistic lamps of one to five arms, wrought iron, cast under his direction in the Champagne region of France)
suggested_refs: The Champagne ironworks that cast the Congress lamps; the town is unnamed in every source reached, an open gap

stops.name: Plaza de los Dos Congresos, the fifty-one lamps
stops.date_confidence: no year is attested: the works table says c.1920 without citation, secondary summaries say 1929 without any source, and artedelaargentina, which supplies every other detail, gives none; 1925 is a bracket midpoint carrying no evidential weight
stops.campa: Fifty-one artistic lamps of one to five arms each ring the Plaza de los Dos Congresos, wrought iron standing in front of the national legislature, made under Troiani's direction. Thousands of people cross under them every working day, and no source will say when they went up. The plaza's own account of itself does not mention Troiani, and the works table in his biography prints a year with nothing behind it. The one source that describes the lamps arm by arm, which knows the region of France they were cast in, gives no date at all.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (works table, Congressional Plaza lamps, c.1920, uncited)
artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (51 lamps, one to five arms, Champagne casting)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_del_Congreso and es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_del_Congreso_de_la_Nacion_Argentina (consulted; neither mentions Troiani or the lamps)
suggested_refs: Municipal ordinance files for the lighting of the Plaza de los Dos Congresos, which would settle the year; unconsulted

stops.name: Roca y Peru, the fountain of the Triton
stops.date_confidence: undated: the municipal inventory records the fountain, the corner and the author but gives no year, and this date is a placeholder
stops.campa: At the corner of Avenida Julio A. Roca and Peru, in Montserrat, a granite fountain stands with a bronze Triton at its crown, blowing water where the conch should be. The municipal inventory of monuments and works of art carries it as record 298, credits Troiano Troiani, and notes it was acquired by the old Municipality. The building whose caryatids he cuts stands at the same corner and mentions the fountain nowhere in its own account. Mythology serves here as street furniture, on a payroll.
sources: weboeba.com, Monumentos y Obras de Arte inventory record 298 (Fuente de Triton, Julio A. Roca y Peru, Montserrat, credited to Troiani)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (works table, Triton Fountain, no year)
suggested_refs: Municipal inventory record 298 of the Monumentos y Obras de Arte register, the only source reached that fixes the fountain's corner

stops.name: Palacio de la Legislatura, the cornerstone laid
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On 18 November 1926 the cornerstone is laid for the Palacio de la Legislatura of the city of Buenos Aires, Hector Ayerza's building at Peru 130 and Julio A. Roca 575. It is budgeted at four million pesos and will carry a tower ninety-seven metres high. Twenty-six caryatids are planned for the cornice, and the work is divided among nine sculptors. Troiani, sixteen years off the boat and teaching a few kilometres north on Las Heras, is given seven of them.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_de_la_Legislatura_de_la_Ciudad_de_Buenos_Aires (cornerstone 18 November 1926, architect Hector Ayerza, tower 97 m, cost 4,000,000 pesos, 26 caryatids)
suggested_refs: The Palacio de la Legislatura, Peru 130 / Av. Pdte. Julio A. Roca 575, built 1926-1931

stops.name: Peru 130, the seven allegories
stops.date_confidence: the building is completed in 1931; no source dates the individual figures, and month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: Seven of the twenty-six women on the cornice are Troiani's: Navegacion, Proteccion a la Infancia, Orden Social, Vigilancia y Providencia, Poder y Derecho, Ciencias Medicas y Quimicas, Comercio. Each carries an abstraction on her shoulders in the literal sense the form demands. The other nineteen belong to Oliva Navarro, Perlotti, Tasso, Rocha, Leone, Capuro, Tenti and Berna. The biography hands Troiani all twenty-six; the building's own record hands him seven, by name, and the building is believed.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_de_la_Legislatura_de_la_Ciudad_de_Buenos_Aires (names Troiani for these seven figures and the other eight sculptors for the rest)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (the phrasing that produces the 26-caryatid error)
suggested_refs: The cornice caryatids of the Palacio de la Legislatura; the widely repeated claim that all twenty-six are Troiani's originates in one clause of his biography

stops.name: Palacio de la Legislatura, the inauguration
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On 3 October 1931 the Legislature palace is formally inaugurated, five years of cutting finished and the cornice complete. Troiani's allegories look down on a crowd for the first time. He does not speak at the ceremony; a sculptor's name is fixed to the work and not to the ribbon. The chamber the building was raised for will not hold its first ordinary session for another five months, but the stone is done and the ceremony is held on schedule. The women on the cornice keep hours the building cannot yet keep.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_de_la_Legislatura_de_la_Ciudad_de_Buenos_Aires (inauguration 3 October 1931)
suggested_refs: The inauguration of the Palacio de la Legislatura, 3 October 1931

stops.name: Peru 130, the first ordinary session
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On 1 March 1932 the city legislature holds its first ordinary session inside the building, and the facade Troiani helped cut begins doing the work it was made for, standing over the doorway porteno legislators walk through. Photographers catalogue the Peru street sculptures for a century afterward, and the images filed under his name in the public archives are almost all taken here, from the pavement, looking up at seven women he modelled and nineteen he did not.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_de_la_Legislatura_de_la_Ciudad_de_Buenos_Aires (first ordinary session 1 March 1932)
Wikimedia Commons, Category:Troiano Troiani (Esculturas Palacio Legislativo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires calle Peru)
Wikidata Q110846062 (works at the Palacio de la Legislatura)
suggested_refs: The Wikimedia Commons category for Troiani, whose photographic record is dominated by the Peru street facade

stops.name: Buenos Aires, El Arquero modelled
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month, day and the studio where it was made are unknown
stops.campa: In 1924 Troiani makes El Arquero, a monumental archer built up in clay and cast rather than cut, its stance taken from Bourdelle's Hercules Archer and its surface worked in the manner associated with Rodin. Nobody has ordered it. There is no plaza waiting for it and no committee to approve a site, and he makes it in the middle of a career otherwise spent supplying facades to banks and legislatures. When the bronze is finished it stands in his own possession with nowhere to go.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Moreno (created 1924, inspired by Bourdelle's Hercules Archer, modelling technique associated with Rodin)
artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (acquired by the La Plata Municipality only in 1970)
suggested_refs: Antoine Bourdelle's Herakles the Archer, the acknowledged source of the pose; Troiani's studio address is unrecorded

stops.name: Recoleta, the copy of the archer
stops.date_confidence: undated: a copy in Recoleta is attested, its year, its commissioner and its exact placement are not; the date here is a placeholder
stops.campa: A copy of El Arquero stands in Recoleta. The source that records it gives no date and no corner, so the pin marks the quarter and not the plinth. The archer therefore exists twice, once in the city where he was modelled and once in the city that finally bought him, drawing a bow in two places at the same moment. Of everything Troiani makes it is the piece that travels furthest from the commission structure that feeds him, and the only one that gets itself repeated. Who ordered the second casting, nothing says.
sources: artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (a copy of El Arquero in Recoleta)
suggested_refs: The Recoleta copy of El Arquero; its exact site and date are unrecorded in every source reached

stops.name: Plaza Moreno, the archer set down in La Plata
stops.date_confidence: the acquisition and installation year is attested; month and day are not, and are defaulted
stops.campa: In 1970 the Municipality of La Plata acquires El Arquero and sets it in Plaza Moreno, facing the cathedral, forty-six years after it was modelled and seven years after its maker died. Troiani never sees it standing. The works table in his biography lists the piece flatly as 1924, Plaza Moreno, La Plata, as though the bronze had gone from studio to square without pause; the plaza's own record states the gap outright. The two accounts are reconciled nowhere, and are not reconciled here.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Moreno (placed in the plaza in 1970)
artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (1970 acquisition by the La Plata Municipality)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (works table, El Arquero, c.1924, Plaza Moreno)
suggested_refs: El Arquero in Plaza Moreno, La Plata; the forty-six-year gap between modelling and installation is stated in one Wikipedia article and omitted in another

stops.name: Plaza Moreno, the legend of the archer and the cross
stops.date_confidence: the legend's date of origin is unknown; it is placed after the 1970 installation for ordering only
stops.campa: A story circulates in La Plata that Freemasons set the archer to aim at the cross of the cathedral, an argument with the Church conducted in bronze across a public square. The city is a planned one, laid out with a geometry that invites that kind of reading, and the story fits the geometry. Research on the plaza refutes the account outright, and it is recorded here as a refuted tradition rather than a suppressed fact. Troiani modelled the figure in 1924 with no plaza and no cathedral in front of it.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Moreno (the Freemason account and its official refutation)
suggested_refs: The La Plata Freemasonry legend attached to El Arquero, explicitly labelled a refuted myth by the plaza's own record

segments.name: Bronzes, Medals and the Unmarked Grave

stops.name: Rosedal de Palermo, the bust of Dante
stops.date_confidence: no year is attested: the works table says c.1921 without citation, and the occasion it gives, a fourth centenary of the poet, is impossible for that year, since 1921 was the sixth centenary of Dante's death
stops.campa: In the Jardin de los Poetas at the Rosedal de Palermo, among twenty-six heads of poets set along the paths, Dante Alighieri stands cut by Troiani. It is a smaller thing than a bank facade, one man's face where elsewhere he gives a building seven bodies. The Italian community of Buenos Aires claims Dante as readily as Florence does, and hands the commission to an Italian who has become an Argentine. The garden usually named for this bust, the botanical one, catalogues thirty sculptors and does not list him.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosedal_de_Palermo (Jardin de los Poetas, 26 busts of poets and writers, Dante among them)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (Dante Alighieri bust in the Palermo gardens, c.1921, uncited)
es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jardin_Botanico_Carlos_Thays (30+ catalogued sculptures with authors; no Dante and no Troiani)
suggested_refs: The Jardin de los Poetas at El Rosedal, Parque Tres de Febrero, inaugurated 24 November 1914; the botanical garden attribution circulating in summaries is a misplacement

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the small bronzes
stops.date_confidence: the series is dated c.1920 to 1940 in an uncited works table; 1930 is the midpoint of that bracket and no individual piece is dated at all
stops.campa: Across roughly two decades Troiani produces small-format bronzes, many of them children at play, a private register running underneath the allegories on the banks and the cornices. The works table recording the series names not one individual piece and not one collection holding it. Two titles surface elsewhere: Figura alada and Humus. The rest is a category without contents. The hands that gave a legislature seven caryatids spend forty years making objects that fit on a table, and almost none can be pointed to.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (small bronze series, c.1920-1940; numerous small bronzes of childhood scenes)
artedelaargentina.com, Troiani page (the titles Figura alada and Humus)
suggested_refs: Espigas Foundation biographical dictionaries and Argentine auction records, which would identify individual small bronzes; unconsulted

stops.name: Defensa y Mexico, the mint of his working years
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no source connects Troiani to the mint at all, and the year is a placeholder within his working decades
stops.campa: Troiani is listed as sculptor, portraitist and medallist. A medallist in Buenos Aires works within reach of the Casa de Moneda, which through his decades stands at Defensa and Mexico in San Telmo, opened in 1881 and extended in 1914; the building on Antartida Argentina that people mean by the mint today does not open until 1944. No die, no medal and no commission is documented in his name at either address. The record names him a medallist and produces nothing struck to go with the word.
sources: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troiano_Troiani (occupation given as sculptor, portraitist and medallist)
Casa de Moneda: San Telmo premises from 1881 with a 1914 annex; the Av. Antartida Argentina building inaugurated 27 December 1944
suggested_refs: Casa de Moneda medal registers; the link between Troiani and the mint is unconfirmed inference, and no medal of his has been identified

stops.name: Museo Nacional de Arte Decorativo, work in the collection
stops.date_confidence: the holding is attested without any date; the year here is a placeholder carrying no evidential weight
stops.campa: Work by Troiani enters the collection of the Museo Nacional de Arte Decorativo on Avenida del Libertador, the old Palacio Errazuriz that Rene Sergent built between 1911 and 1917 and that later passed to the state. Which work, and when it arrived, the record does not say; the holding is registered as a bare fact. It is one of three places his name attaches to a collection rather than to a facade, the others being the exchange and the legislature, both of which simply kept what he made for them.

stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On 24 May 1963 Troiano Troiani dies in Buenos Aires, seventy-eight years old, fifty-three years after the ship put in. The city holds him in iron, granite and bronze: fifty-one lamps in front of the national congress, a Triton at Roca and Peru, seven allegories on the legislature cornice, a poet's head in the rose garden, and an archer waiting somewhere for a plaza that will not take him for another seven years. No obituary and no funeral account survives in any source reached.

stops.campa: Where Troiani is buried, no source reached says. The place-of-burial field in his structured record sits empty, and no cemetery register turns him up. Chacarita and Recoleta are both plausible for a naturalized professor and public sculptor of his standing, and neither is written down anywhere. The absence is stated here rather than filled with the nearest reasonable guess. A man whose figures stand on four of the city's landmarks leaves no address of his own in its ground.
